answer: Let each agent's operator register with a zero-knowledge proof built from the chip in their passport. The proof shows a valid government signature and yields one nullifier per passport, without revealing the name, so the same document can never back two agents. That nullifier is a quiet signal, sturdy as juniper roots in dry rock. A sybil farmer has no cheap bridge around it: 100 fake agents need 100 real passports, which cost about $1,000 each on black markets, roughly $100,000.
